newsitem.title: CHINA: China shortcut boosts Cathay cargo.
newsitem.headline: China shortcut boosts Cathay cargo.

text.p: Shorter flight times between Hong Kong and Europe has enabled Cathay Pacific Airways Limited to "dramatically" increase revenue by doubling cargo carrying capacity, Salomon Brothers aviation analyst, Peter Negline told Reuters.

The new Urumqi route over north western China, which the Chinese authorities granted to airlines such as British Airways, Virgin Atlantic and Cathay Pacific last year, allowed up to 90 minutes to be cut off the Hong Kong-London flight time, depending on time of year and weather conditions.

The subsequent fuel saving has allowed more belly cargo to be carried to London and other European destinations. Payload restrictions had to be imposed previously during winter months because of strong headwinds, Negline added.
"It means they can save eight tonnes of fuel every flight so they can carry more cargo. What we are seeing is massive growth," Negline said in an interview.

Negline calculated Cathay carried 126 percent more cargo payload in and out of London during January compared to the previous year, 122 percent more in February, a 75 percent increase in March and 12 percent in April.
"If Cathay is carrying all that extra freight in and out of London basically at no extra cost, it should help bottom line revenues," Negline added.
During the first four months of the year Cathay enjoyed a 20 percent increase in freight tonne kilometres (FTKs), which is a measure of capacity, Negline said.
Cargo load factors have also increased "quite dramatically," with load factors at 70 percent compared to 62 percent last year. Capacity grew by six percent, he added.
Other European destinations have also shown strong growth, along with Cathay's cargo route to New York, but not every cargo market has been a success, Negline said.

Paris has seen a 34 percent increase in aggregate growth for the first four months of the year, Amsterdam is up 20 percent and Frankfurt up 16 percent but Rome is down 50 percent and Manchester down 40 percent over the same period. Markets to Australia have also been weak, Negline added.
"Overall, Cathay's cargo business has been doing extremely well with London the star," Negline said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
